summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with sepsis likely due to a urinary tract infection caused by ESBL-producing E. coli, presenting with respiratory failure, hypotension, and altered mental status. She was intubated and treated with meropenem. During her ICU stay, she developed coagulase-negative staph bacteremia from a line, managed with linezolid after line removal. ARDS and pulmonary edema improved with supportive care. Her mental status cleared after reducing methadone and stopping sedatives. Renal function normalized despite a non-obstructing kidney stone. She completed antibiotics, was extubated, and regained mobility. Warfarin was restarted with lovenox bridging. She was discharged to extended care for rehabilitation with stable infections and therapeutic INR.
